theme: 3 terms on sorting rules: largest first, keeping ties in their old order, and the rule every sort comparison has to follow

terms.definition: Sorting from the largest value to the smallest, so the biggest item comes first.
terms.example: Show the scores in Descending Order, so the winner is at the top.

terms.definition: A sort that keeps items that compare as equal in the same order they had before sorting.
terms.example: Swift's `sort` is a Stable Sort, so messages with the same time keep their order.

terms.definition: The rule a sort comparison must follow, for example an item never comes before itself.
terms.example: Less than or equal isn't a Strict Weak Ordering, so the sort result isn't guaranteed.

quizzes.question: What do you call a sort that keeps equal items in the order they came in?
Which rule says a sort comparison must never put an item before itself?
In this code, which order puts the biggest score first?

video.title: Descending Order, Stable Sort & Strict Weak Ordering | Day 73
video.description:
Learn to explain sorting rules in Swift: Descending Order, Stable Sort & Strict Weak Ordering, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Descending Order - Sorting from the largest value to the smallest, so the biggest item comes first.
Stable Sort - A sort that keeps items that compare as equal in the same order they had before sorting.
Strict Weak Ordering - The rule a sort comparison must follow, for example an item never comes before itself.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

한국어: 내림차순: 가장 큰 값에서 가장 작은 값 순서로 정렬해서 가장 큰 항목이 맨 앞에 오는 것

Strict Weak Ordering - The rule a sort comparison must follow, for example an item never comes before itself.
한국어: 엄격한 약순서: 정렬 비교가 지켜야 하는 규칙으로, 예를 들어 어떤 항목도 자기 자신보다 앞에 올 수 없음

landscape.hook: One extra symbol breaks the sorting rules. Can you explain why in English?

dialogue.title: Greater or equal?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, can you check `top`? Most played songs first.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sure, that's Descending Order. But why greater than or equal?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So songs with the same `plays` keep their order.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That breaks the rule. Swift's sort needs a Strict Weak Ordering.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What does that mean in plain words?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A song must never come before itself, but greater or equal says it does.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The order isn't guaranteed. Use greater than, a real Strict Weak Ordering.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: But then I lose the order of the ties.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, `sorted` is a Stable Sort. Ties stay in the order they came in.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nice. Greater than for Descending Order, and the Stable Sort handles ties.
Leaderboards use Descending Order, the best score goes first.
